title: Periodic Motion & SHM — 50 MCQs
description: 50 MCQs covering periodic motion concepts and SHM with explanations. Choose an option, submit to view explanation and mark, then navigate.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of simple harmonic motion?
options: The acceleration is proportional to displacement
The total energy varies with time
The frequency is independent of amplitude
questions.explanation: In SHM, total mechanical energy remains constant (kinetic + potential energy is constant).

questions.q: The time period of a simple pendulum is T. If the length is increased by 300%, the new time period will be:
questions.explanation: T ∝ √L. If length becomes 4L (300% increase), T becomes √4 T = 2T.

questions.q: A particle executing SHM has amplitude A and time period T. The minimum time taken to travel from x = 0 to x = A/2 is:
questions.explanation: Using x = A sin(ωt), when x = A/2, sin(ωt) = 1/2 ⇒ ωt = π/6 ⇒ t = T/12.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle in SHM is given by x = A sin(ωt + φ). Its kinetic energy will be maximum when:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is maximum when potential energy is minimum, which occurs at the mean position (displacement = 0).

questions.q: Two springs of force constants k₁ and k₂ are connected in series. The equivalent spring constant is:
questions.explanation: For springs in series, 1/k_eq = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ ⇒ k_eq = k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂).

questions.q: A simple pendulum is suspended from the ceiling of a lift. When the lift is falling freely, the period of the pendulum becomes:
options: Same as when lift is stationary
questions.explanation: In free fall, effective g = 0, so T = 2π√(L/g) becomes infinite (pendulum doesn't oscillate).

questions.q: A mass m is suspended from a spring of constant k. The system is set into oscillation with amplitude A. The maximum speed of the mass is:
questions.explanation: Maximum speed v_max = Aω = A√(k/m), where ω = √(k/m).

questions.q: The displacement of a particle in SHM is given by x = 5 sin(2πt + π/4). What is the magnitude of maximum acceleration?
questions.explanation: Maximum acceleration a_max = ω²A = (2π)² × 5 = 20π² m/s².

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude A. At what displacement from the mean position is the kinetic energy equal to the potential energy?
questions.explanation: When KE = PE, total energy E = 2PE ⇒ ½kA² = 2 × ½kx² ⇒ x = A/√2.

questions.q: A mass-spring system oscillates with frequency f. If the mass is increased by 300%, the new frequency will be:
questions.explanation: f ∝ 1/√m. If mass becomes 4m (300% increase), f becomes f/√4 = f/2.

questions.q: The total energy of a particle executing SHM is E. When it is at half the amplitude, its kinetic energy is:
A simple pendulum has time period T. If it is taken to a planet where acceleration due to gravity is one-fourth of Earth's, its new time period will be:
questions.explanation: T ∝ 1/√g. If g becomes g/4, T becomes 2T.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle in SHM is given by x = A cos(ωt). The velocity when displacement is A/2 is:
A spring of force constant k is cut into two equal parts. The force constant of each part is:
questions.explanation: For a spring, k ∝ 1/length. When cut into two equal parts, each has half the length, so force constant becomes 2k.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 5 cm and frequency 2 Hz. Its maximum acceleration is:
questions.explanation: a_max = ω²A = (2πf)²A = (4π)² × 5 = 80π² cm/s².

questions.q: Two springs of force constants k and 4k are connected in parallel. The effective spring constant is:
questions.explanation: For springs in parallel, k_eq = k₁ + k₂ = k + 4k = 5k.

questions.q: The time period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m is approximately:
A particle executes SHM with time period T. The time taken to go from mean position to half the amplitude is:
questions.explanation: x = A sin(ωt). When x = A/2, sin(ωt) = 1/2 ⇒ ωt = π/6 ⇒ t = T/12.

questions.q: The potential energy of a particle executing SHM is maximum when:
questions.explanation: Potential energy U = ½kx² is maximum when displacement x is maximum.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM according to equation x = 10 sin(πt + π/3) cm. Its phase at t = 1 s is:
The displacement of a particle in SHM is given by x = A sin(ωt). Its average speed over one oscillation is:
questions.explanation: Total distance in one period = 4A. Time = T. Average speed = 4A/T.

questions.q: A simple pendulum is taken from Earth to Moon. Its time period on Moon compared to Earth will be:
questions.explanation: T ∝ 1/√g. Moon's g is less than Earth's, so T increases.

questions.q: A mass-spring system has time period T. If the spring constant is quadrupled, the new time period is:
questions.explanation: T ∝ 1/√k. If k becomes 4k, T becomes T/2.

questions.q: The acceleration of a particle in SHM is:
options: Always directed away from mean position
questions.explanation: In SHM, acceleration a = -ω²x, always directed towards mean position.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude A and angular frequency ω. Its maximum velocity is:
questions.explanation: Maximum velocity v_max = Aω.

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length L has time period T. If length is increased to 9L, the new time period is:
questions.explanation: T ∝ √L. If L becomes 9L, T becomes 3T.

questions.q: The phase difference between displacement and velocity in SHM is:
questions.explanation: If x = A sin(ωt), then v = Aω cos(ωt) = Aω sin(ωt + π/2). So phase difference = π/2.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with time period 2 seconds. Its frequency is:
The total energy of a particle executing SHM is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Total energy E = ½kA² ∝ A².

questions.q: A simple pendulum executes 40 oscillations in 80 seconds. Its time period is:
questions.explanation: T = total time / number of oscillations = 80/40 = 2 seconds.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle in SHM is given by x = 0.1 sin(100πt) m. Its frequency is:
A mass-spring system oscillates with amplitude A. If amplitude is doubled, the total energy becomes:
questions.explanation: E ∝ A². If A becomes 2A, E becomes 4E.

questions.q: The phase difference between acceleration and displacement in SHM is:
questions.explanation: a = -ω²x. The negative sign indicates phase difference of π.

questions.q: A simple pendulum has length L and time period T. If length is reduced to L/4, the new time period is:
questions.explanation: T ∝ √L. If L becomes L/4, T becomes T/2.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 10 cm. The distance traveled in one time period is:
questions.explanation: In one time period, particle goes from mean to extreme and back twice: 4 × amplitude = 40 cm.

questions.q: The time period of a simple pendulum is independent of:
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g) is independent of mass of bob.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with time period T. The ratio of time taken to travel from extreme to mean position and from mean to extreme position is:
questions.explanation: Both take equal time (T/4) due to symmetry of SHM.

questions.q: A spring-mass system has time period T. If both mass and spring constant are doubled, the new time period is:
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k). If both m and k are doubled, ratio m/k remains same, so T remains T.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude A. Its speed is half the maximum speed when displacement is:
questions.explanation: v = v_max√(1 - x²/A²). When v = v_max/2, √(1 - x²/A²) = 1/2 ⇒ 1 - x²/A² = 1/4 ⇒ x²/A² = 3/4 ⇒ x = A√3/2.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle in SHM is x = 8 sin(πt + π/6) cm. Its displacement at t = 0 is:
A simple pendulum is taken to a height equal to Earth's radius above Earth's surface. Its time period compared to on Earth's surface will be:
questions.explanation: At height h = R, g' = g/(1+h/R)² = g/4. T ∝ 1/√g, so T becomes 2T.

questions.q: Two springs of force constants k₁ and k₂ have equal maximum extension under same force. Their potential energy ratio is:
questions.explanation: F = kx, so x = F/k. For same F, x ∝ 1/k. PE = ½kx² = ½k(F²/k²) = F²/(2k). So PE ∝ 1/k. Ratio = (1/k₁):(1/k₂) = k₂:k₁.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude A. The mean position of velocity over one oscillation is:
questions.explanation: Velocity is a sinusoidal function. Mean value over one complete cycle is zero.

questions.q: A mass m is suspended from a spring of constant k. The system oscillates with frequency f. If another mass m is added, the new frequency is:
questions.explanation: f ∝ 1/√m. If mass becomes 2m, f becomes f/√2.

questions.q: A simple pendulum has time period T in air. When completely immersed in water, its time period:
questions.explanation: In water, effective g decreases due to buoyancy, so T increases.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle in SHM is given by x = A sin(ωt) + B cos(ωt). The amplitude of motion is:
questions.explanation: x = √(A²+B²) sin(ωt + φ) where φ = tan⁻¹(B/A). So amplitude = √(A²+B²).

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with time period 6 seconds. The minimum time after which its kinetic energy becomes 3/4 of total energy is:
questions.explanation: KE = (3/4)E when PE = E/4 ⇒ x = A/2. Time from mean to A/2: t = T/12 = 6/12 = 0.5 s.

questions.q: A simple pendulum is vibrating in an elevator. If elevator accelerates upward with acceleration a, the time period becomes:
questions.explanation: In accelerating elevator, effective g = g + a (upward acceleration). So T = 2π√[L/(g+a)].

questions.q: A mass-spring system oscillates with amplitude A. If amplitude is halved, the maximum acceleration becomes:
questions.explanation: a_max = ω²A ∝ A. If A becomes A/2, a_max becomes a_max/2.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM according to x = A sin²(ωt). This represents SHM with amplitude:
questions.explanation: x = A sin²(ωt) = (A/2)(1 - cos(2ωt)) = A/2 - (A/2)cos(2ωt). This is SHM about x = A/2 with amplitude A/2.
